notes: JCPenney Home (jcpenney.com), dept20000011 = the Home department node. Discovery: the Home department page's own server-rendered nav links to '/g/home-store?s1_deals_and_promotions=CLEARANCE&id=dept20000011' with analytics tags literally reading '...FTH_SalesPromotions_Clearance...' and '...DEPT-FTH-_-VN-24-_-Clearance...' - the site's own taxonomy explicitly labels this Clearance (not a generic Sale/Offers page), satisfying the brief's Clearance-vs-Sale test. Opened via Claude-in-Chrome (client-rendered, so counts aren't in raw HTML - see Access note): the page title is 'Home Clearance', it shows 5 circular navigation tiles (Bedding, Home Decor, Luggage & Bags, Home Closeouts, Shop All Clearance) plus, below the tiles, a real filtered product grid with an active 'CLEARANCE' facet chip reporting 'Filter 157 results' - this 157 is the site's own reported count for the Home-scoped Clearance concept and is used as the parent qty (superseding an earlier direct Constructor.io API guess of 144, which is now understood to have been an incomplete facet-count approximation - the live rendered grid is authoritative). Genuine children (each opened, each carrying its own active 'CLEARANCE' filter chip): Bedding Clearance (33), Home Decor Clearance (73), Luggage Clearance (18). A 5th tile, 'Home Closeouts', uses a distinct deals_and_promotions value (CLOSEOUT! rather than CLEARANCE) - opened and confirmed it is a real PLP (page title 'Home Closeout Sale | Furniture, Mattresses, & More', 194 results, products carry a red 'CLOSEOUT!' badge with dramatic permanent-looking markdowns e.g. a Beautyrest mattress crossed out from $1,800-$2,800 to $299-$719) - included as a clearance-style listing (permanent markdown/end-of-line stock) per the brief's Outlet/End-of-Line/Discontinued equivalence, but flagged since the site's own label text is 'Closeout' rather than one of the brief's literal listed terms. The 6th tile, 'Shop All Clearance', links to a SITE-WIDE clearance page (id=cat1007450013, not dept-scoped) - excluded as out of this company's Home-only scope (matches the prior Home-Decor pass's note that this sitewide URL exists separately). Child counts do not sum to the parent (33+73+18=124 vs 157) - expected, since other Home sub-departments (e.g. Kitchen, Bath, Lighting) evidently also carry some clearance stock without having their own dedicated tile in this particular hub; not treated as an error per the brief's overlap guidance. No ambiguous generic-sale pages were mistaken for Clearance: the 'Labor Day Home Sale' and 'Now Trending'/'Liz Claiborne Event' banners seen throughout are clearly temporary seasonal promotions and were not recorded. Access: direct HTTP fetch (tier 1) confirmed nav links, robots.txt (no Claude-specific disallow) and the Constructor.io backend/facet structure; Playwright (tier 2) was blocked site-wide (net::ERR_HTTP2_PROTOCOL_ERROR/ERR_CONNECTION_RESET on every jcpenney.com URL, including robots.txt, while example.com loaded fine - a headless-Chromium bot-detection block, not a general outage), so Claude-in-Chrome (tier 3) was used to render each PLP and read its site-reported 'Filter: N results' text plus the active filter chip as evidence.
